result.title: How Does Geometry Enter Generated Motion?
result.comment: 43 pages, 13 figures, including supplementary material. Project page: https://liweihan1107.github.io/samelaw/
result.summary: Under a fixed physical law, the visible geometry of a scene determines how motion must change. We ask how video generators realize this relationship. We fix the law and the initial state and change only the geometry drawn in the first frame, within matched families of tracks and deflectors, and compare each generated trajectory with the simulator prediction for that geometry. Paired interventions change one thing at a time: a local bump, the height of a barrier, the words of the prompt, the length of the clip. Across nine image-to-video models, geometry is preserved and shapes the motion: the speed of the ball follows the drawn undulation of a track. A physical state would carry this response forward, and here the generated motion parts from the law. The mean slope barely accelerates the ball, successive contacts fail to compose through a consistent state, an edit ahead of the ball alters its motion before it arrives, and the ball climbs over barriers higher than its release point. Two global conditions organize the global trajectory: text strongly controls the destination, while clip length strongly controls timing in the open-weight models tested. The pattern persists with photographed first frames. Current video generation thus behaves as geometry-conditioned motion synthesis whose evolution of state differs systematically from that of a fixed physical law.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在固定物理定律与初始状态、仅改变首帧几何（轨迹与挡板）的受控干预下，比较九类图像到视频模型生成轨迹与模拟器预测，发现几何能塑造运动，但模型缺少一致的物理状态演化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「几何条件化运动合成、状态不成立」的诊断可能启发 LVR 中「视觉旁路」与内部状态是否真正承载任务必要几何信息的问题，可核查其对未来编辑、接触组合的失配是否类比于 latent 状态的因果作用缺失。
